question: Your support agent sets tool_choice to {"type": "tool", "name": "get_customer"} on the first request of each refund conversation. Logs show that get_customer is now always called first. However, that response ends with stop_reason "tool_use" after the single call, and your code treats it as the final response, so no refund is ever processed. Which change best lets the workflow continue while keeping get_customer as the guaranteed first step?

options.text: Send the whole conversation as one Message Batches API request, so that the get_customer call and the refund steps are processed together.
options.reason: The Message Batches API has no multi-turn tool calling support, so the follow-up turns that process the steps after get_customer cannot run in it.

options.text: Raise max_tokens on the first request, so that the model has room to call lookup_order and process_refund after get_customer in the same response.
options.reason: The response did not stop for lack of tokens; it ended with the forced tool call and stop_reason "tool_use". The later steps belong in follow-up turns, so a larger max_tokens does not continue the workflow.

options.text: Remove the forced selection and add a system prompt rule to call get_customer first, so that the model can continue the workflow on its own.
options.reason: A prompt instruction does not guarantee that get_customer is called first, so it loses the guarantee that forced selection gives. It also does not fix the code that stops after the first response.

options.text: Return the get_customer result in a follow-up request with tool_choice set to "auto", and keep looping while stop_reason is "tool_use".
options.reason: Forced selection guarantees only the first call. The later steps are processed in follow-up turns, stop_reason "tool_use" means the loop must continue, and "auto" lets the model then choose lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human or a text reply.
